Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-08-12 | AAPL | Underweight | +4.8% | +5.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Reduce AAPL to 50–75% of a standard allocation: sell 25–50% of current exposure now into 302.25, leaning to the larger end if the position is at or above standard weight, and sell more into any rally to 309.5–311.4 (trim further toward 317.19 if volume fails to confirm the lift). Do not initiate new long capital below 311.4, and do not take the trader's tactical short at 302.25 — the stop at 311.5 is only ~1.1 ATR (8.55) inside normal noise and the payoff is ~1.4:1. Risk controls: a close below 300.00 on >55M shares cuts further, then 295.18; a close below the rising 200 SMA at 280.09 invalidates the primary trend and prompts exit of the residual. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three seats converge on reducing AAPL exposure and disagree only on whether to convert that into a short and on re-entry mechanics; the bear case wins on forward risk/reward but not by enough to justify liquidation, hence Underweight rather than Sell.

The deciding evidence is distribution, not momentum decay. The 2026-07-31 session gapped 333.43 to a 304.81 open and closed 308.91, −7.35% on 132.5M shares (~2.4x average); the subsequent bounce to 313.33 drew only 34.4M shares before rolling to a lower low at 300.57 against 302.56. Lower highs at 314.81 → 309.97 → 305.66 confirm a downtrend channel. At 302.25, AAPL is below the 10 EMA (311.35), the 50 SMA (309.48), the VWMA (317.19) and the Bollinger mid (321.22), so the July cohort is underwater and 309–317 is overhead supply. The 50 SMA has inflected down for the first time in the lookback with the 10/50 death cross ~1.87 points away, MACD is below zero with the histogram re-widening to −3.343, and RSI 40.22 is the lowest of the 40-session lookback but not oversold. This is materially different from the 2026-07-20 through 07-24 AAPL Underweights that each bled +3.2% to +3.8% of five-day alpha by selling momentum decay inside a stacked rising structure — this sells after a printed volume-distribution day and a failed bounce, the exact distinction the 2026-07-30 lesson (which earned −9.9% alpha) codified. Equally, the 2026-08-05 Overweight reflection — do not deploy even a starter before the confirmation gate triggers while the histogram widens negative — forbids buying here.

Forward-model risks all lean one way and remain unresolved: inventory +94% to $11.1B with raw materials +260%, a ~$13.3B gross-intangible step-up implying $1.3–2.6B/yr of amortization into FY2027 operating income (so 32.62% is not the forward margin base), effective tax rate up 219bp to 17.58%, R&D +32.5% versus revenue +16.4%, and buybacks cut 12% while FCF rose 52% with $48.8B parked in securities — management's own capital allocation declining to buy its stock at these prices. Gross margin at a record 50.06% against opex growth of ~22% versus revenue ~16% means the entire operating-margin expansion rests on one line item that memory/component costs can reverse, and the confirming print is not until late October.

Where the bear overreaches, and why this is Underweight not Sell: the business is not impaired — revenue $109.4B +16.4%, 50.06% gross margin, nine-month FCF $110.2B, net cash ~$62.2B, $14.4B of debt retired with zero new term debt, current ratio back above 1.0x — and price sits 7.9% above a rising 200 SMA at 280.09. The aggressive analyst's tactical short at 302.25 is the weakest proposal in the debate and the other two seats are right to reject it: the 311.5 stop is ~1.1 ATR inside single-session noise, a 2.3–3.1% rebound fills it, the payoff to 289 is only ~1.4:1, and shorting a 0.136 %B print just above the 300.00–302.56 shelf after an 11.12% nine-session drawdown bets that the next leg arrives before a normal rebound. The death cross is lagging and its stop sits exactly where the plan declares the bearish thesis wrong. Sizing guidance: express bearishness by being liquid at 285–295, not by adding gap and headline risk; any tactical short requires a failed retest of 309.5–311.4 or a close below 300 on >55M shares, at half the normal risk budget or less.

What would change it. Upgrade to Hold/Overweight on a daily close above 311.4 on >55M shares, with a close above 317.19 on volume read as trend repair and a hold of the 321–325 confluence plus readable intangible/inventory footnotes justifying a rebuild toward standard weight. Move toward Sell on a decisive close below 300.00 on >55M shares, then 295.18; a sub-48% gross-margin print with a soft FQ4 guide converts this to Sell. A 25–33% starter in 285–295 is permitted only for mandates explicitly allowing value entries, conditional on stabilization there (reversal candle or bullish RSI divergence on heavy volume) with invalidation below 280.09 — not an automatic dip-buy. Stated gaps: no consensus forward EPS or revision trend, no valuation multiple, no options chain or implied move, no sentiment data, a news sample of 20 records, and no portfolio context — so all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation, and 289 is a technical congestion target, not valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 289.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
Five days delivered +4.8% raw and +5.3% alpha versus SPY, so the Underweight call was directionally wrong in this window — the trim at 302.25 sold into what became outperformance — though five days cannot adjudicate a 1–3 month thesis built on an October print.

The distribution/overhead-supply case (309–317 as supply, death cross pending, histogram re-widening) is what this window undercuts, and price evidently probed the 311.4 close-on-volume gate the plan itself named as the upgrade trigger; what it supports is the rejection of the tactical short at 302.25 with a 311.5 stop, which would have been stopped out inside the same move.

The concrete lesson: an Underweight whose falsification level sits only ~3% above entry has poor expectancy, so next time size the rating by distance-to-invalidation — at that proximity the honest call was Hold with a sell-into-317 plan, not a 25–50% reduction.

[2026-08-11 | AAPL | Underweight | +1.7% | +2.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Trim AAPL by 35–40% now — roughly two-thirds at market near 304.91, with at most one-third left as sell-limits into 311.50–314.00 — bringing total exposure to about 60–65% of the caller's benchmark AAPL weight. Hedge the residual core with a put spread (or a cost-effective collar if vol is cheaper there) sized to residual notional around the 297.91–300 zone, and size the residual off the actual ~12.6-point distance from a 304.91 reference to the 317.50 invalidation, not the trader's 6.0-point unit, with ATR at 8.81 (2.89% of price). Put no new money to work until a daily close above 313.37 on >65M shares and then above 318.14 on expanding volume. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print, with a hard review line at a weekly close below 297.91.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is not contested — the aggressive, conservative and neutral seats all land on SELL as the transaction, and the Research Manager's plan is Underweight. The debate is about degree and execution, and that is where the call is made.

The reduce case wins on the only forward-looking evidence, and it wins decisively. The bull material is real but dated: Q3 FY26 revenue +16.4% to $109.42B, gross margin 50.05%, EPS +28.7%, nine-month FCF $110.2B, net cash $62.2B. All of that was public before 2026-07-31, when AAPL gapped −8.58% and closed −7.35% at 308.91 on 132.5M shares, roughly 2.6x the ~50.8M average — the market pricing the 10-Q, not missing it. What matters since: a bounce from 08-04 to 08-07 on 68.0M → 49.4M → 46.1M → 34.4M shares, weakest volume on the highest close (313.33), then lower highs at 313.33 → 308.26 → 304.91. Fading volume on a rising sequence after an earnings-gap distribution is no-bid. Price at 304.91 sits below the 10 EMA (313.37), 50 SMA (309.56), 20 SMA (322.48) and VWMA (318.14), so the volume-weighted holder is underwater 4.16% overhead; the 50 SMA slope has collapsed from +0.79 to +0.03 points/day, the 10 EMA has fallen eight straight sessions, MACD crossed below zero (+0.072 → −0.827) with the histogram re-widening to −3.271, and the 10/50 bearish cross is one to three sessions away. RSI 41.92 offers no oversold cushion, so the neutral's own 45% chop / 35% down / 20% up mix yields negative expected value from here. The forward pressures the bull never answered are the ones that matter: memory/component costs management itself called unsustainable to absorb, the Jefferies downgrade to Underperform at a $263.66 target (13.5% below spot), inventory +93.9% with raw materials +260%, buybacks down ~12%, an effective tax rate up 219bp, and a ~$4.9B pre-tax / ~$0.28 EPS hit per 100bp of gross-margin compression — roughly 8% of EPS on a 250bp reversal, before any multiple compression.

Where each seat overreaches. The aggressive is right on direction and right that exit liquidity is above, not below, but wrong to dress a trim as a trade: off a 304.91 reference with a 317.50 invalidation the risk is 12.59 points against 6.91 to the 298 target — about 0.55:1, not the 2.3:1 claimed — and the neutral's catch that the 6.0-point risk unit is inconsistent with a 317.50 stop is correct and adopted. The aggressive also turns the 279.87 200 SMA into a target; it is a stress reference and a sizing input, not a forecast. The conservative wins the execution argument outright — do not build the plan around a second bounce the market has already refused to deliver — but pushing to a 60–65% cap immediately, at the lower end of a still-valid range with a 45% chop base case and light follow-through (44.8M and 37.5M), over-de-risks. The neutral is the most balanced and supplies the two best mechanical corrections (stop/risk-unit mismatch; put spread likely cheaper than a collar given post-gap implied vol), but its 30–35% trim is too timid for this trigger. My own record settles degree: the 07-20 to 07-27 Underweights each forfeited 3.2%–3.8% of five-day alpha by trimming intact uptrends on momentum decay alone, while the 07-29 and 07-30 Underweights that worked (−13.6% and −9.9% alpha) were anchored to a dated catalyst and an actual distribution print — and the 07-29 lesson was explicit: when the anchor is a real trigger, take the larger de-risk. The 08-04 Hold lesson applies too: do not price a mid-range posture as free; commit the invalidation level in advance.

Why Underweight and not Sell: the primary structure is intact — AAPL is 8.95% above a rising 200 SMA at 279.87, the 50 remains above the 200, and the balance sheet and cash conversion are not impaired — so a full exit would abandon a core worth keeping through a 45%-probability chop scenario. Why not Hold: the distribution trigger has printed, the probability mix is negatively skewed, and a benchmark-weight posture here would repeat the GOOGL error of absorbing the full downside passively.

What would change it: stand down and restore toward benchmark weight on a daily close above 313.37 on >65M shares, confirmed above 318.14 on expanding volume; cut again on a high-volume (>~70M) close below 300.00; move toward Sell on Q4 gross margin ≤47.5%, inventory >$13B at 2026-09-30, or a heavy-volume break of 297.91; rebuild toward a constructive stance only on Q4 revenue >$105B, gross margin ≥49.5%, inventory <$8B and net cash >$65B. Stated gaps, not papered over: no valuation multiples, no options chain or implied-vol data (hedge cost must be checked before execution), no Q4 consensus, a news sample with no coverage of 08-04 to 08-09, and no knowledge of the caller's holdings or cash — hence sizing as a fraction of the caller's own benchmark AAPL weight, and the $290 target is technical, not valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 290.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day +2.1% alpha versus SPY shows the Underweight call was directionally wrong, but five sessions are too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis. This window undercuts the fading-volume/distribution premise, since price did not follow through lower after 304.91, while supporting the refusal to go full Sell as the intact primary structure absorbed the pressure. Next time, require a confirmed close below the stated 300/297.91 trigger before taking the larger de-risk rather than acting on volume decay alone.

[2026-08-10 | AAPL | Underweight | -0.9% | -0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL: trim roughly one-third of the position at or near $308.26, leaving ~2/3 of the caller's standard AAPL weight — partial de-risking ahead of a probable test of the $300–302.56 floor, not an exit. Do not put on the aggressive analyst's tactical short at spot (a 316.29 stop is ~0.9 ATR and sits inside one normal session); if a hedge is mandated, wait for a decisive close below $304.61 or preferably $300.00, cap it at ~1/4 standard, and stop above $319.09 (~1.5 ATR). Hard trim trigger: decisive close below $300.00 on >60M shares → cut another third to ~1/3 standard; re-add in two tranches only on a close above $316.29 with >60M shares and the 10 EMA ($315.25) reclaimed, then above VWMA $319.09. Do not average down in the $304–$308 no-man's-land. Size stops off ATR ≈ $8.94 (1.0–1.5 ATR), never sub-1 ATR. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the Q4 FY2026 print in late October.

**Investment Thesis**: The bear wins the 1–3 month horizon on measured tape evidence, the bull wins the long term on uncontested fundamentals, and neither wins decisively enough for a binary exit. All three risk seats converged on reducing exposure — aggressive "trim plus short," conservative "trim, no short," neutral "trim, staged re-add" — and the neutral construction is the one that survives because it is the only one that both honors the deterioration and prices the hedge correctly.

What decided the direction. (1) The technical structure is the best-evidenced part of the debate: seven sessions without a close above the 10 EMA at $315.25, a failed 50 SMA reclaim ($309.70 versus a $308.26 close on 2026-08-10), lower highs at $316.29 → $314.81 → $308.26, monotonically decaying bounce volume from 75.0M to 34.4M, VWMA at $319.09 marking trapped supply ~10.8 points overhead, and MACD at 0.072 versus a 3.26 signal with the histogram at −3.19 heading toward a zero-line cross. RSI 44.10 offers no oversold cushion and Bollinger %B at 18.6% with expanding bands means breaks follow through rather than mean-revert. With ATR at $8.94 (2.90% of price), the triple-tested $300–302.56 floor is roughly one ordinary session away. (2) The aggressive analyst's one real overreach was caught by both other seats: a 316.29 stop from a 308.26 entry is ~0.9 ATR — inside one normal daily range and just under the zone where stops cluster — and the payoff only reaches 1:3 if you assume the floor breaks and AAPL travels to $294–289 or $279.64. At the first target ($299.53) it is ~1.1:1 before slippage. So the short overlay is not the expression of this edge; the trim is. (3) The market already saw the same 10-Q the bull cites and gapped −7.35% on 132.5M shares (~2.6x average), unrepaired for seven sessions — at roughly 34x trailing, good numbers were priced, which is the neutral's point that we cannot demonstrate "fully priced" without valuation multiples but can demonstrate that the marginal buyer did not show up. (4) Margin durability is a genuine open risk, not a headline: 50.06% gross margin reverting toward 47.5% costs ~6–8% of EPS, and the memory cost cycle carries a 1–3 quarter lag, with Q3 ending June 27 before the August cost reporting.

What kept this at Underweight rather than Sell. The fundamentals are not in dispute: revenue +16.1%, gross margin 49.07% (+225bps), Q3 gross margin 50.06%, diluted EPS +22.4%, FCF +52.5%, cash conversion 1.15x, receivables −21% on higher revenue, net cash +$62.17bn, debt −$14.31bn, D/E 0.78x, dividend payout 11.6%, and a Q3 buyback rebound to $25.11bn (+19.1% YoY) that refutes the stale deceleration story. The long-term trend is intact and uncontested — price 10.24% above a rising 200 SMA at $279.64, 50 > 200 positive — and the bear himself said "strategically still bullish." The near-term downside catalyst is also narrative-heavy: three repeats of one WSJ-origin memory report, a speculative iPhone pricing item, and 145 of 165 eligible news records missing; the report's own verdict is "a cost-cycle and narrative risk, not a demand break," and the aggressive analyst never rebutted it.

Prior lessons, applied.
